title: PRD: Consumption Sandbox & Scenario Runner
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This PRD describes the Consumption Sandbox & Scenario Runner: an interactive console feature and API that lets customers simulate realistic workload scenarios to estimate cost, latency, and SLO impact before changing production routing, fidelity, or capacity commitments. The sandbox runs closed simulations against anonymized performance profiles and optional captured traces so teams can validate configuration changes (batching, quantization, model variant mixes, routing policies, cache hit-rates) and view forecasted unit economics and reliability trade-offs.

Why we build it
----------------
- Reduce churn and risk for customers migrating from hosted to dedicated/private or changing fidelity/quantization settings.
- Lower support and finance friction by enabling self-serve cost forecasting and preflight validation.
- Improve platform trust: customers can preview how SLOs, tail latency, and cost per token change across scenarios.

Goals (measurable)
------------------
1) Reduce time-to-decision for fidelity and routing changes by 60% for enterprise self-serve flows (measured by time from opening sandbox to completing a purchase/commit change).
2) Surface reliable cost and latency estimates with median error <= 10% vs real workload within first 30 days of rollout (for standard simulation templates).
3) Reduce support tickets categorized as "unexpected cost after change" by 40% in the first 6 months post-launch.

Non-goals
---------
- We will not run live traffic in customer environments or perform destructive tests. The sandbox uses curated performance profiles and optional de-identified traces.
- Not a full fidelity A/B traffic router — it is a planning and preflight tool (not an automated rollout engine).

Primary users / personas
------------------------
- Platform engineers evaluating Dedicated capacity and autoscaling policies.
- Product/ML engineers tuning model variants, quantization, or token budgets for routes.
- Finance/Procurement teams estimating monthly spend under hypothetical usage profiles.
- Solutions engineers who run scenario runs with customers during onboarding.

Core use cases
--------------
1) Fidelity trade-off: simulate cost and latency when moving 30% of requests from variant-v1 (fp16) to variant-v2 (quant-4).
2) Capacity planning: estimate required dedicated GPU pools for an expected 2M monthly tokens with P95 latency <= 450ms.
3) Routing policy experiment: simulate splitting by latency vs cost and see per-route SLO attainment.
4) Cache effectiveness: project token cost savings at different prefix cache hit rates.

Functional requirements (high-level)
-----------------------------------
- FR1: Scenario definition UI and API where customers provide: workload shape (RPS vs time), request mix (route IDs, prompt length distribution, model variant mix), duration, and configuration toggles (batch size, kv-cache enabled, quantization profile, fallback policy).
- FR2: Prebuilt templates for common scenarios: bursty mobile chat, steady throughput embedding ingestion, mixed chat+generation.
- FR3: Simulation engine that consumes Redwood performance profiles and optional de-identified traces to produce per-scenario metrics: estimated monthly token count, projected compute-hours, cost estimate (hosted/dedicated billable model), P50/P95/P99 latencies, expected SLO violations, and suggested autoscaling knobs.
- FR4: Visual reports: charts for cost over time, latency distribution, per-route breakdown, and a table of recommended configuration changes with estimated delta.
- FR5: Exportable reports: PDF and JSON outputs suitable for procurement or internal review.
- FR6: RBAC: only users with appropriate console permissions can run scenarios for a tenant; allow read-only sharing links for stakeholders.
- FR7: Persisted scenarios with versioning and ability to snapshot current production config for comparison.

Non-functional requirements
---------------------------
- NFR1: Interactive scenario runs for small-to-medium workloads should return an initial estimate within 20s (P50) and a full simulation within 3 minutes (P95).
- NFR2: Batch-run simulation queue for large/long scenarios; asynchronous completion notifications via console and webhook.
- NFR3: Accuracy target: median absolute percent error <= 10% for cost, <= 12% for P95 latency for scenarios built from standard templates and performance profiles.
- NFR4: Data retention: stored scenario inputs and outputs retained 365 days; remove de-identified traces after 90 days unless customer opts-in.
- NFR5: Audit trail: every scenario run must record user, changed parameters, and snapshot of performance profile id.

Success metrics (KPIs)
---------------------
- Adoption: % of enterprise customers who run at least one scenario during onboarding (target 70% within 90 days).
- Forecast accuracy as defined in NFR3.
- Business impact: % reduction in "unexpected cost" tickets and % increase in dedicated-reservation conversions after using sandbox.

UX flows and wireframe notes
---------------------------
1) Create scenario: guided modal with 4 steps (Workload, Model & Routing, Fidelity & Runtime, Run & Report).
2) Quick-start templates available in the top-right, with one-click populate.
3) Run view: progress bar, streaming log of assumptions, estimated running cost updates, cancel button.
4) Results page: KPI summary card, visual charts, side-by-side compare to baseline (production snapshot).
5) Actionable buttons: "Apply to staging rollouts", "Export PDF", "Open support ticket with scenario".

API / CLI example
------------------
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/scenarios \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"mobile-chat-burst","duration_minutes":60,"workload":{"rps_profile":"burst","peak_rps":1200},"routes":[{"route_id":"chat-main","model_variant":"gpt-small-quant4","percent":100}],"preferences":{"batch_size":16,"kv_cache":true}}'

Sample scenario YAML (console export)
-----------------------------------
name: mobile-chat-burst
duration_minutes: 60
workload:
  rps_profile: burst
  peak_rps: 1200
routes:
  - route_id: chat-main
    model_variant: gpt-small-quant4
    percent: 100
preferences:
  batch_size: 16
  kv_cache: true
  fallback_policy: regional-fallback

Simulation engine design (overview)
----------------------------------
- Input: scenario descriptor + optional de-identified traces captured from customer's route(s).
- Selector: map model variant + hardware target to a curated performance profile (compiled from our perf-suite).
- Event generator: expand the RPS/time profile into synthetic requests using sampled prompt-length and tokenization distributions.
- Cost estimator: per-token compute model with adjustments for batching, cache hit-rate, quantization multipliers, and autoscaling efficiency losses.
- Latency model: probabilistic per-token latency distribution derived from kernel-level profiles, with tail amplification under high concurrency.
- Output aggregator: produce time-series and summary metrics plus recommended knobs.

Performance profiles and inputs
-----------------------------
We will maintain a catalog of performance profile artifacts for supported model variants and hardware classes. Each profile contains: average tokens/sec, batching efficiency curve, p50/p95 token latencies, memory usage, and quantization multipliers.

Telemetry and observability
--------------------------
- Emit scenario_run.* metrics to internal telemetry: duration_seconds, estimated_cost_usd, median_error_estimate, profile_id_used.
- Link simulation outputs to the customer's cost dashboard and a trace id for audit.
- Track downstream conversions: dedicated reservation conversions attributed to a scenario run id.

Rollout plan
------------
Phase 0 (internal): 4 weeks — implement engine with default templates, internal-only console flag.
Phase 1 (pilot): 8 weeks — invite 10 enterprise customers (Solutions-led). Collect feedback and measure accuracy targets.
Phase 2 (general availability): 6 weeks post-pilot — open to all enterprise customers; provide training docs and sales enablement.
Phase 3 (self-serve): 12 weeks — expose limited feature set to SMB customers with guardrails and cost-visibility limitations.

Operational runbooks (summary)
-----------------------------
- If simulation queue latency > 90th percentile target: scale simulation workers (runtime team).
- If forecast error drifts > 15% for a given profile: create a profiling task to refresh the performance profile (ML infra).
- If customers report confidentiality concerns: check trace anonymization pipeline and retention policy (security + legal).

Open questions / decisions to make
--------------------------------
1) Allowed level of customer-supplied traces — will we accept raw logs (opt-in) or require SDK-backed capture?
2) What billing model (if any) for heavy asynchronous simulation runs? free vs per-simulation credit model.
3) How to surface confidence intervals for users in a way that avoids paralysis-by-analysis?

Appendix: configuration table (recommended defaults)
---------------------------------------------------
| Setting | Default | Notes |
| batch_size | 8 | Default works for most chat workloads; increase for throughput-heavy embedding jobs |
| kv_cache | true | When enabled, estimate cache hit-rate at 30% unless customer supplies trace |
| quant_profile | quant-4 | Safety default; allow quant-2 in advanced templates |
| fallback_policy | model-fallback | Options: model-fallback, regional-fallback, degrade-to-hosted |
| autoscale_efficiency | 0.85 | Multiplier applied to ideal autoscale to reflect cold-starts and fragmentation |

Appendix B: Example output schema (JSON)
----------------------------------------
{
  "scenario_id": "string",
  "summary": {
    "estimated_monthly_cost_usd": "number",
    "estimated_p95_latency_ms": "number",
    "expected_slo_violations": "number"
  },
  "time_series": ["timestamped-metrics"],
  "recommendations": ["list-of-textual-recs"]
}
